title: 深海生物の適応とトレードオフ
sourceLabel: 既存教材をTOEFL形式へ変換 · 元の問1–9に対応
verificationNote: Editorial answers（編集・確認した解答）。元の本文・解説に基づき記述設問を英語4択へ変換しています。元記事の記述問題も引き続き利用できます。

passages.text:
The deep sea is not one uniform habitat, but much of it combines high hydrostatic pressure, low temperature, little or no sunlight, and limited food. Pressure rises by roughly one atmosphere for every ten meters of depth. It does not simply squeeze an animal from the outside like a hand crushing an empty container, because tissues contain water and internal pressure is also transmitted. The biological problem is subtler: pressure can alter molecular volumes, membrane behavior, and the shapes or reactions of proteins. A trait that helps a membrane remain functional at depth therefore addresses a cellular constraint, not merely a problem of body strength.

Darkness creates a different set of constraints. Below the sunlit layers, photosynthesis cannot supply most local food webs. Organic particles and bodies sink from above, animals consume one another, and chemosynthetic production supports particular habitats such as vents and seeps. Food delivery is uneven in space and time. Many deep-sea species have traits consistent with limited energy, including slow growth, infrequent feeding, or low routine activity. These are tendencies, not rules for every species. A predator that waits for rare prey and an animal living beside a productive vent face different energy budgets even at similar depths.

Bioluminescence shows why function must be inferred carefully. Producing light can help an organism lure prey, communicate, find a mate, confuse an attacker, or reduce its silhouette by matching faint light from above. Yet a flash may also reveal the producer to an observer able to detect it, and chemical production or control of light requires resources. Researchers therefore examine the position of light organs, the timing and wavelength of emission, behavior before and after a flash, and the visual systems of other organisms. Finding a luminous organ demonstrates capacity; it does not, by itself, establish one exclusive function.

Finally, organisms did not acquire these traits because they understood what the deep sea required. In evolutionary adaptation, inherited variants differ in survival or reproduction under particular conditions, and their frequencies can change across generations. An individual may also acclimate within its lifetime, but acclimation is not the same process. Every specialization has boundaries: molecules stabilized for high pressure may perform differently when pressure falls, weakly mineralized or gelatinous tissues can aid buoyancy but do not maximize rapid, forceful swimming, and a low-energy strategy can limit growth or recovery. Adaptation is therefore not perfection. It is a historically produced compromise that must be tested against a specified environment and outcome.

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the passage?

options.label: A
options.text: Every organism in the deep sea uses the same set of adaptations.

options.label: B
options.text: Deep-sea traits should be linked to specific constraints, evidence, and costs rather than treated as perfect solutions.

options.label: C
options.text: The main challenge at depth is that water crushes every animal with an empty body cavity.

options.label: D
options.text: Bioluminescence has one universal function that can be identified from anatomy alone.

questions.answer: The passage treats adaptations as conditional benefits with limits and costs. 正解：B。Aは生息地の違い、Cは細胞分子への圧力作用、Dは発光の複数機能を無視します。constraintは「働きや可能性を制限する条件」です。

questions.prompt: Why is body strength alone insufficient to explain adaptation to high pressure?

options.label: A
options.text: Pressure cannot enter tissues, so only the animal's outer surface is affected.

options.label: B
options.text: Pressure is identical at every depth, so strength has no relationship to the environment.

options.label: C
options.text: Pressure is transmitted within water-containing tissues and can alter membranes and proteins, making cellular function a central issue.

options.label: D
options.text: Pressure affects only empty body cavities and leaves all molecular processes unchanged.

questions.answer: Internal pressure is transmitted too, and molecular effects can change cellular function. 正解：C。第1段落は空の容器のように潰れるという比喩の限界を示します。A・Dは分子への作用を消し、Bは水深に伴う圧力増加に反します。membraneは「細胞膜」です。

questions.prompt: In paragraph 4, the word 'compromise' is closest in meaning to

options.label: A
options.text: a trait with benefits, limits, and costs under particular conditions

options.label: B
options.text: an organism consciously choosing the best possible body

options.label: C
options.text: a change that improves every biological function equally

options.label: D
options.text: a feature that appears without inheritance or selection

questions.answer: A compromise works under some conditions while retaining limits and costs. 正解：A。compromiseはここでは「利益と制約が両立する折り合い」です。Bは意識的選択、Cは全機能の完全な向上、Dは遺伝と選択を除外し、進化説明と合いません。

questions.prompt: Which pair of reasons explains why low activity is not a rule for every deep-sea species?

options.label: A
options.text: Pressure is constant, and all species receive food directly from sunlight.

options.label: B
options.text: Every species can choose its food supply, and all vents stop producing energy at night.

options.label: C
options.text: Bioluminescence supplies all food, and organisms at the same depth must have identical lifestyles.

options.label: D
options.text: Food supply varies across places and times, and species with different lifestyles can face different energy budgets even at similar depths.

questions.answer: Food delivery is uneven, and a waiting predator differs from an animal near a productive vent. 正解：D。第2段落は供給条件と生活様式の両方を示します。A〜Cは光や食物供給を誤り、個体が供給を選べるとも述べません。energy budgetは「得られるエネルギーと消費の収支」です。

questions.prompt: Why does finding a light-producing organ not establish one unique function for it?

options.label: A
options.text: Light organs demonstrate that the animal can never be detected by other organisms.

options.label: B
options.text: Light can serve several purposes, so organ position, emission, behavior, and other organisms' vision must be examined to distinguish functions.

options.label: C
options.text: An organ's appearance always proves that its only purpose is attracting a mate.

options.label: D
options.text: Researchers cannot observe any behavior before or after a flash.

questions.answer: Several functions are possible, and context is needed to distinguish them. 正解：B。第3段落の誘引・通信・繁殖・防御などは候補で、器官だけでは決められません。Aは被発見リスクに反し、Cは唯一の機能を断定、Dは行動観察を否定します。emissionは「光などを発すること」です。

questions.prompt: Which observation is NOT among those the passage proposes for investigating bioluminescence?

options.label: A
options.text: when the light is emitted

options.label: B
options.text: behavior before and after emission

options.label: C
options.text: the visual sensitivity of nearby organisms

options.label: D
options.text: whether all deep-sea species share an identical genome

questions.answer: Timing, behavior, and other organisms' visual systems are explicitly relevant. 正解：D。全深海種が同一ゲノムを共有するかは観察項目に含まれません。A〜Cは発光と相手の反応を結び付ける検証です。visual sensitivityは「どの光を検出できるかという視覚の感度」です。

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly distinguishes evolutionary adaptation from acclimation?

options.label: A
options.text: Adaptation involves changes in inherited-variant frequencies across generations; acclimation occurs within an individual's lifetime and is not the same process.

options.label: B
options.text: Adaptation is an individual's deliberate choice, whereas acclimation requires all species to share one genome.

options.label: C
options.text: Adaptation occurs only within one lifetime, whereas acclimation always changes inherited-variant frequencies across generations.

options.label: D
options.text: Both terms mean that an acquired physiological change must be inherited unchanged by every offspring.

questions.answer: Adaptation concerns inherited variation across generations; acclimation concerns change within a lifetime. 正解：A。第4段落は時間尺度と遺伝の位置付けを区別します。Bは目的論、Cは逆転、Dは獲得した状態の必然的な遺伝を付け足します。acclimationは「個体の生理的な順応」です。

questions.prompt: Which statement best paraphrases 'Finding a luminous organ demonstrates capacity; it does not, by itself, establish one exclusive function'?

options.label: A
options.text: Finding the organ proves that every flash increases survival in every environment.

options.label: B
options.text: The organ's presence proves a single function, so behavioral evidence is unnecessary.

options.label: C
options.text: The organ shows an ability to produce light, but identifying what the light does in context requires additional evidence.

options.label: D
options.text: The organ provides no evidence of light-producing ability unless all neighboring species also have one.

questions.answer: Capacity is what the animal can do; function is what that ability accomplishes in context. 正解：C。capacity（能力）とfunction（実際の働き）では証拠が示す範囲が違います。A・Bは効果や唯一性まで飛躍し、Dは能力を示すという前半を否定します。exclusiveは「それだけが唯一の」です。

questions.prompt: Which revision best replaces the claim that a fish 'decided to save energy' with the passage's evolutionary explanation?

options.label: A
options.text: The fish understood food scarcity and deliberately passed its chosen metabolic rate to its offspring.

options.label: B
options.text: Inherited low-energy variants could become more common if they improved survival or reproduction under scarce food; this explanation requires comparative evidence and must account for possible costs to growth or recovery.

options.label: C
options.text: All fish at the same depth acquired the same slow metabolism immediately because pressure instructed their cells to change.

options.label: D
options.text: A slow metabolism must maximize every function, so measurements of food, inheritance, and reproductive success are unnecessary.

questions.answer: Inherited differences may spread through differential survival or reproduction, not conscious decisions. 正解：B。元の発展記述の進化機構・比較証拠・費用を保持します。A・Cは必要を理解して変化する目的論、Dは検証とトレードオフを消します。metabolic rateは「代謝率」、reproductive successは「繁殖成功」です。
